Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing questions

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NovaClinic is interested in an on-prem VPC deployment but we need more flexibility on the platform fee and SLA while we ramp. Two quick asks:

1) Can the platform fee be staged (amortized) over 12–24 months rather than paid fully upfront?
2) If we commit to a 24-month term, what discount and SLA improvements can you offer vs. a short pilot?

High level context: we expect production traffic in Q4 and would like a 3–6 month pilot window, then scale. Budget team needs a clear amortization path to justify the initial outlay. I attached a short requirements doc so you can see our timeline.

Attachments: NovaClinic_requirements_v1.docx (see timeline section)

Would appreciate a short write-up of options we can share with procurement by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
NovaClinic Health

--
Elena Mendez
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged licensing and SLA tradeoff for VPC

Elena — thanks for the clarity and the timeline. Summary below with two pragmatic paths; I'll follow up with Marissa for numbers and Sean for final approval.

Option A — Pilot-first (lower upfront, limited SLA)
- 3–6 month pilot, monthly metered billing for token usage + small pilot platform fee (credited if convert)
- SLA: best-effort during pilot; 99.9% target only once committed term begins
- Benefit: minimal initial capex; trade-off is higher unit rates and no premium SRE on-call during pilot.

Option B — Staged commit (amortized platform fee, stronger SLA)
- 12–24 month committed license where platform fee is amortized across invoices (we can do quarterly amortization)
- If you sign 24-months: conditional discount applied (we need exec finance sign-off; Marissa to propose bands)
- SLA: 99.95% with a named SLO and on-call during business hours for 12+ month committed terms. Higher tiers (24–36 months) unlock 24/7 on-call.

Next steps: Marissa will share a short pricing matrix (platform fee, support tier options, and example amortization). If that looks acceptable, I can loop Sean to approve the conditional discount and Karthik/legal for a short amortization clause in the SOW.

I attached a short one-pager (pricing-options-summary.pdf) to make this easy for procurement.

Thanks,
Irene
Senior Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Elena / team — attaching a compact pricing table and SOW sketch (sow_and_pricing_table.xlsx). Highlights below — these are illustrative and we can tailor.

Platform fee options (annualized equivalent):
- Pilot (3–6m): one-time pilot fee $15k + metered usage rates (no platform amortization)
- 12-month staged: platform fee $96k (can invoice quarterly $24k)
- 24-month staged: platform fee $168k (equivalent annual $84k; we can amortize quarterly)
- 36-month anchor: platform fee $240k (we can structure as 12/12/12 tranches)

Support tiers (examples):
- Bronze: Business-hours support, 24h response for sev1, no on-call ($0 additional)
- Silver: 24/7 monitoring + 4h sev1 response + named SRE during business hours (+10% platform fee)
- Gold: 24/7 SRE on-call + 1h sev1 response + quarterly ops review (+25% platform fee)

Discount / concessions guidance:
- 24-month commit: typical conditional discount 10–15% off platform fee (requires finance approval)
- 36-month commit: can push to 18–22% with PoC acceptance clause and early-sign bonus
- Pilot-to-commit: pilot fee credited 50% to the first committed period if signed within 90 days

I've attached the spreadsheet with line-item math and a sample amortization schedule. If you want, I can convert this to a redlineable SOW for legal.

Attachments: sow_and_pricing_table.xlsx

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Staged licensing and SLA tradeoff for VPC — SLA tradeoffs and fallback

Team — quick operational note on SLA tradeoffs and how we should structure fallback if NovaClinic chooses a lower commit: 

Proposed SLA matrix (text):
- Commit >= 24 months AND platform fee >= $150k: 99.95% availability, 24/7 SRE, 1h sev1 response
- Commit 12–24 months AND platform fee between $80k–$150k: 99.9% availability, business-hours SRE + on-call, 4h sev1 response
- Pilot / Commit < 12 months: 99.5% availability, best-effort on-call, 24h sev1 response

Fallback / risk controls:
- Elastic routing: if we detect production spike > planned capacity, auto-fallback to hosted tier for X hours (charges apply) — avoids escalations during pilots
- Credit mechanics: platform fee amortization requires a clause where early termination triggers a prorated repayment of the unamortized portion or reduction of discounts

Operational ask from engineering: if NovaClinic expects cold-start edge deployments in region-us-west, we should require a 2–4 week onboarding window for dedicated cache warming (can be included in SOW).

I've exported the SLA matrix (sla_matrix.csv) and cc'd Sean for commercial sign-off on the discount bands.

David
Director, Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
